text: Widows without sons or brothers had almost no way to earn a living. The believers’ daily distribution was meant to reach every one of them (Acts 4:34).
Stephen sends you with bread and oil to a widow from Alexandria who lives alone in two rooms near the Fish Gate. She speaks Greek. You speak it badly.
You stumble through a prayer in Greek. Halfway through she takes over and finishes it for you.
Nothing miraculous happens in Miriam’s two rooms. A widow eats, and she is not alone. Stephen says that is what the Seven were chosen for.
Before you go, you pray with her.
You have bread, oil, and the rest of the afternoon.
Yesterday. A little. Do not trouble yourself.
She sits very straight and waits for you to speak.
You write MIRIAM OF ALEXANDRIA in your best hand. She watches you do it as if it were a deed to land.
Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, give I to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
